facts.core: Metal (the cells are written for every chart with a Metal core; no number, band or state of one chart in any value)

angles.drive: You compete best with someone to beat and know it. Knowing where you stand matters more than comfort, so you compete harder against one rival than for any reward. Pick one contest with a finish line, because yours have no end in sight.
angles.cost_self: Without a rival, you lose your pace. Competing keeps you going, and the next round comes ahead of noticing you are tired. Compete against your own record for a month, since you never reach a finish that lets you rest.
angles.cost_others: For you, competing with a friend is taking them seriously. You raise the stakes out of wanting someone worth beating more than someone easy to keep. Keep one friend outside the contest, as you cost a rival the ease of siding with you.

angles.drive: Your yes to a bet comes before the fear has finished. Hesitating feels like losing to yourself, so you bet first and size it afterwards. Keep one bet a year you can afford to lose, since nerve costs you money as much as pride.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the stakes go up, you are first to bet. Betting first is the closest you get to sure, and you size it to nerve rather than savings. Size one bet to the savings, because the early yes costs you money put aside.
angles.cost_others: Betting first is your way of carrying the people who hesitate. By betting for the group instead of asking it, you put their money where your nerve is. Check the size with them first, before you spend their caution like your own courage.

angles.drive: You trust a person faster when the risk is shared. Sharing the risk makes the bond real to you, so you go in together ahead of writing anything down. Write the terms down once, because you risk the friendship as much as the money.
angles.cost_self: Where a friend needs backing, you share the risk first. Sharing the risk feels closer than staying out, and the shared bet comes before your margin. Keep one account no friend can draw on, since you cover their losses with money meant for rest.
angles.cost_others: Sharing a risk with someone is your warmest offer. Wanting them in it more than safe from it, you share the upside and the fall. Say the downside first, as you bring the people you like into risks sized to your nerve.

facts.pair_definition_catalyst: Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Metal makes it hard, and your will holds. Running thin, strength gives out, so you manage alone rather than lean on a peer and bet big instead of resting. You last longest once you let rest and company in.
facts.pair_advise_catalyst: You treat rest as something you earn after the work instead of the thing the work runs on. Take rest in first and sleep before the hard decision rather than after it. Let one peer carry a job you could do yourself. Sit out one contest a month on purpose. Eat before you answer the message.
facts.claim_fixed: How to use Metal, the Body energy.
